answer: The total strength of the magnetic field varies smoothly across the land, forming contours that a survey has already mapped. A magnetometer reports the total field intensity, and the verifier checks it against the contour map for the claimed area, so a glacier valley, a grove of walnut and a ridge where a falcon hunts each sit on a different contour. A farm can measure one contour value, but it cannot place a thousand accounts on a thousand different contours from a single spot.
